# Invoke-ZbxCheckNow

## SYNOPSIS

Asks the server to check items now.

## SYNTAX

```
Invoke-ZbxCheckNow [-InputObject] <ZabbixReference<ZabbixItem>[]> [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

The Invoke-ZbxCheckNow cmdlet asks the server to poll the items given to -InputObject (names, ids or piped items) at once, rather than at their next scheduled check, with task.create; it is the frontend's Execute now. Only polled items can be checked now; a trapper, dependent or active agent item cannot. The command writes the id of each task it created, which Get-ZbxTask reads, and -WhatIf shows what it would ask.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Check an item now

```powershell
Get-ZbxItem -Host 'web-01' -Name 'Uptime' | Invoke-ZbxCheckNow
```

The task runs on the server (or the host's proxy) within a few seconds; the new value arrives as usual.

### Example 2: Check now and follow the task

```powershell
$taskId = Get-ZbxItem -Host 'web-01' -Name 'Uptime' | Invoke-ZbxCheckNow
Get-ZbxTask -Id $taskId | Select-Object TaskId, Type, Status
```

Get-ZbxTask reads the task the command created; Status shows whether it ran.

## INPUTS

- `ZabbixReference<ZabbixItem>[]`: Bound to -InputObject (ByValue). Represents a reference to an API object: a parameter that points at an API object takes its id, its name, or the object itself piped from a Get- cmdlet, and becomes an id before the call — one parameter, three spellings, one resolution.
